dnd/dnd-2025-01-12-session-notes.title: January 12, 2025 - Session Notes
dnd/dnd-2025-01-12-session-notes.content:
Recap

From fire was unable to enter any of the places I needed to go.
My Patron did some weird shit and infuriatingly insisted on the 5 questions format even when not needed.
Was told that I needed to go and help my friend, but confusingly my patron doesn’t care even remotely about my friends.
Asked how I can meet with my patron in person and was given a door knob and a mask.
Was taken to Breeze’s village where he had been teleported and immediately gotten in to trouble and ran up a tree.
Helped smooth things over with Breeze’s tabaxi family, and told his mother about what happened with his brother. He doesn’t know.
We were sent to the front line where we found out that the big fire that was being blamed by both elves and tabaxi on the other side, was actually an enormous robot army of unknown allegiance.

Today’s session
Anwynn and Breeze

Breeze and I continuing to travel with the tabaxi towards the front lines, hoping to get some answers out of them and observe the warforged, before losing them and crossing the lines during the night.
Get taken by (Shadow of the) Hunter and (Hunters) Mark to meet with a tabaxi in the dress of the Gaia clergy.
Supported Breeze in trying to trick the tabaxi.
Succeeded a deception check to explain away why I have a cloak her recognised as being worn by another in his order.
Succeeded in getting Breeze to not do anything stupid.

Ivir and Rafross

Ivir makes a whole lotta noise using Thaumaturgy to attempt to call to all the animals charging at the enemy.
Some scouts from the human kingdom jumped out of the trees attempting to stop him.
The leader of the scouts agree to give two of his number to watch over the army of warforged overnight while the rest go with Ivir to convince the elves to let those fleeing through the wall.

Gladys

Has finally made it to her village and her people.
Is welcomed to a ragtag group of leaders, representing all the different familys/groups in the camp.
Aiden is a hothead wood elf who is just angry and aggressive about being locked out of the wall, and is upset at Gladys for not seemingly doing enough. Is intimidated into silence after being questioned for what he’s actually done.
No one knows why they haven’t been granted passage.
Stefan has spoken to military people in charge of the wall but have just delayed and not said anything concrete.
Discussing how to force their hand to get passage for the people in the camp.
Helga a forest gnome who seems very cool. Ripped grandma. “Lets go give them a piece of our mind why don’t we”.
Gladys and the others go up to those in charge of the wall to demand answers.
Helga follows Gladys in sitting on a crate in the middle of a walkway to protest being stonewalled on information.
Others start join in their sit in protest.
Gladys weaponises the small children of her family to bother the guards.
Gladys pulls rank and gets taken inside to talk to the general (Heinrich).
General Heinrich parrots a very rehearsed line about “processing times” and “due processes” that must be followed before any refugees will be allowed in.
Realises that none of the replies to the bureaucratic sendings have been received. This is a surprise to him.
He goes to talk to the wizard and asks Gladys to wait.

At this time it’s the end of the day, Rafross and Ivir are coming close to the wall and Gladys again. Anywnn and Breeeze are settling down to camp before sneaking away.
Back to Breeze and Anywnn

Breeze asks again if we should escape.
Plan to dimension door from the tent off to the side to get as far away from the army as possible.
Get a 20+8 on deception to leave a Gaia symbol on the floor of the tent, succeeding in having them not immediately chase us.
Run into the scouts that were working with Ivir and convince them that we’re trusted. They realise we know Ivir.

All coming together again

Rafross runs ahead of Ivir to watch the chaos unfold.
Ivir, accompanied by a stampede of all the animals of the forest, led in stride by 4 large bears, thunder directly into the middle of the refugee camp.
Gladys sitting in the waiting room.
A wizard comes to talk to Gladys and is imperious and snobby and rude, takes 2 psychic damage when Gladys assets herself as an agent of Marcella.
Heinrich speaks on Gladys’ behalf as well to demand answers from the Wizard.
In the distance Gladys begins to hear Ivirs chanting and the sound of animals stampeding.
Ivir halts his army of animals, and walks authoritatively with his four bears towards the gate.
The sit in flees further inside in the face of the stampede.
Ivir demands for everyone in the camp to be let in, or to talk to the leader of all elves immediately. Guard is incredibly flustered but tries to agree to let him talk to the wizard.
The bears have to stay outside.
Rafross stealthily climbs up the wall and slips into a window, quickly making himself seem right at home.
Obnoxious wizard has an aneurysm at the sight of all the animals.
Rafross, Gladys, and Ivir together manage to talk Wizard Gleeson into being honest.
Gleeson finally tells the truth at last and apparently the elven valley is completely inaccessible and it’s not possible for them to enter the valley, or send magic in or out.

dnd/dnd-2025-03-02-session-notes.title: March 2, 2025 - Session-Notes
dnd/dnd-2025-03-02-session-notes.content:
Ivir, Gladys, and Rafross

Ivir and Rafross tell Gleeson what’s over the hill and what kind of danger they’re in.
Gleeson immediately arcs up and pushes back on being told what to do.
Ivir tries again to warn of the danger and tells him he’s wasting valuable time, succeeds after intimidation check.
Turns to address Gladys specifically and says that he’s willing to negotiate for protection for the refugees outside the gate in return for us fighting with them to fend off the attack.
Gleeson invites the leaders to dinner to discuss the agreement.
Gleeson orders Heinrich to get his men to collect the other leaders, but obviously doesn’t feel confident in his authority.
Ivir and Rafross clock that as much as Gleeson is pissed off he’s holding all his magic back because he realises that it’ll be needed more later. Rafross additionally realises that while moving through the fortress Gleeson is sending a lot of message spells, and that he’s setting a lot up that depends on getting our help.

Annwyn and Breeze

Both have to make a luck roll to see how much trouble we’re in with a tabaxi strolling up to the main gate.
Two wood elves come up and demand answers, just as I finish saying “I know this looks bad but does he look like a soldier???” Breeze dimension doors both of us into the room with everyone else, with Rafross’ hand wraps as a teleportation target.
Breeze mentions “Marcelas bears” and gets punched by Ivir immediately for 5 damage.
Annwyn tells Gleeson about the warforged and the religiously motivated army and that they’re disconnected from most of the Tabaxi.
While this is all happening, Breeze draws the Gaia symbol and compares it to the medallion we got from the assassin and we realise it’s the same.
Rafross gets a 28 perception and realises he has a scroll from our research in the city into the religious symbols found on the underwater statue, and realises its the same language.
Breeze and I work together using this information to try and decipher what the writing on the Gaia symbol says, previously we had deciphered “Rest here Kisha in the embrace/prison of Abzul” Kisha is symbol of all earth and is related to Gaia/is the same as Gaia.
For Gleeson to agree to let the refugees in, he needs us to agree to tear down the barrier.
He’s done a number of experiments on the barrier, non-magical people can walk through but inevitably find themselves lost and confused and turned around. Lesser wizards can push through a little but with great resistance. Gleeson was able to push far enough to approach a physical barrier, but he is no longer able to describe what he saw or felt, which means it can manipulate even his mind.
Gleeson agrees to allocate an officer to oversee the refugees coming into the fort immediately, and Gleeson takes us down a secret passage towards the barrier so that we can start work on bringing it down immediately.
Annwyn pulls mask out. Mask of many faces. Casts contact other plane.

Annwyn: Do you get along well with other divine entities?
Patron: Sometimes yes, sometimes no
Annwyn: Do you feel this? (Annwyn steps forward into the barrier)
Patron: … (Can’t get a response properly, steps back)
Annwyn: Do you want to help tear this barrier down?
Patron: Perhaps, I could help empower your magic, or you could open another way.

Pull out doorknob and start experimenting with it.

Meanwhile the others continue moving forward:

Rafross starts getting hard to see/focus on and is far ahead, but continues going. becomes engulfed in darkness.
Others start facing enormous resistance.
Breeze casts dancing lights to see if they can penetrate into the darkness. The dancing lights are resisting Breeze’s directions to move forward, takes an action instead of a bonus action.
Rafross tells Breeze that he’s pulling on some kind of invisible rope that’s guiding him.
Breeze keeps trying to move but every step forwards somehow ends up taking him backwards.

dnd/dnd-2025-05-11-session-notes.title: May 11, 2025 - Session Notes
dnd/dnd-2025-05-11-session-notes.content:
All at the Wall

Door looks very plain and nondescript.
Insert doorknob, roll 13 on chr arcana check.
Feeling of rightness and familiarity, but unable to remember where from or what exactly the feeling is.
Succeed on a roll to push the door open, with Anwynn subconsciously prioritising getting to their patron.
Door opens into the mysterious travelling house we visited.

Breeze, Rafross, and Ivir Alone at the Wall

Breeze decides to use summon aberration to attempt to summon Starspawn.
Rafross fails history check, but crits on a perception check and finds out that Breeze reached deep into some part of his soul and tore open reality, to the same place that the boggle creatures from the beginning came from.
Rafross gets a 17 on a wisdom save but its not enough.
He can see through the tear but he has such perfect vision of the tear that he can see all possible planes that the tear connects to.
Where this has been summoned from is like one page of the book that’s been torn open, the starspawn emerges and that plane seals behind it.
Rafross is so shaken that he loses the ability to talk or communicate, all ability to use language is gone.
Starspawn attacks the wall with a 15 roll for psychic slam and gets thrown backwards.
Ivir sees the Starspawn attack the wall and get thrown backwards.
Ivir charges up to the wall with his glaive flaming, and succeeds on an attack roll and does, dealing 19 fire damage.
To pull the glaive out of the wall, it feels like pulling through something very thick and heavy and a piece of the thread has pulled out.

Anwynn and Gladys

A tall imposing and powerful but nonthreatening woman steps into the room, with the small reptile creature tucked into a sleeping bag thing on her shoulder.
She sees us and is nonplussed, invites us in for tea.
She complements Gladys on the meal she had started cooking when we were last there.
She starts doing this like boiling water and steeping tea, and though they should take a lot longer, seem to happen instantly.
She locks the pantry and lets Berry out and she Berry immediately runs over to smother Gladys.
Anwynn asks what to call her.
She says that our friends have been calling her Babayaga.
I respond saying that I can use that name but it seems unlikely that Ivir would know her name.
She says that she is “The Patron”, a facilitator of deals.
All of a sudden the tea is gone, but Anwynn and Gladys are satiated.
She tells Gladys not to lose herself in the coming chaos of the world.
Anwynn asks The Patron if she can restore their memories. She says that she can’t but Anwynn is the result of a deal made with an entity that they were once a part of.
They ask her whether they have any regard or loyalties to the planes she exists upon, but she doesn’t, she only exists to make deals.
As a final question/statement Anwynn says that it was good to meet her at last, and that they hope that she doesn’t deal the world into destruction. She responds saying that Anwynn shouldn’t worry and that they’re doing fine.

All at the Wall Again

Rafross attacks the wall again with a 28. Gets a 19 athletics check to break the thread.
At this moment Gladys and Anwynn step back into the scene.
Rafross’ hand wraps are falling apart even more with each attack. As the thread snaps they unravel even more.
We all feel an otherworldly pulse of power.
Breeze feels thorny brambles harden around him.
Rafross can feel the woven wall which is only tangible to him, fall over and smother him. Not unpleasant but overwhelming.
After this pulse we see a 16 ft figure with scaly skin that more resembles cracked earth, the same figure as the statue underwater.
It’s Gaia/Kishar.
She seems mad.
“And after I gave you all such a lovely wish…”

Fight Begins

Rafross confidently strides up to her and punches, rolling a 25 with a stunning strike. Gaia passes the con save on stunned. Deals 13 damage regardless.
Attacks again with another stunning strike, does 8 damage but the stunning strike fails again.
Rafross only comes up to her hip at best.
Gaia’s turn, “really, this is what destroyed my wall, you’re all sooo small”
She summons an earthen hand that attacks Rafross. He just manages to push it aside and avoids its damage.
Anwynn tries to cast faerie fire on her but it fails.
Breeze’s turn and he asks why we wouldn’t want to tear the wall down. She responds “You don’t like being contained?”
Breeze attacks for 23 points of psychic damage, and she is forced her reaction to move directly away from Breeze.
Ivir hits with an opportunity attack for 18 damage.
She uses a legendary reaction to teleport right on top of Gladys.
Ivir moves in, powering up his glaive, and attacks with smite, dealing 38 damage, passes strength saving throw.
She seems fine.
Ivir feels like he ran into a wall.
He attacks again for another 27 damage.
She attacks Ivir and he takes 19 halved to 9 damage.
Gladys uses fire magic for 19 damage.
Rafross hexs her for wisdom checks.
Then hits for 9 force damage and 1 necrotic. Exactly the same again on opportunity attack.
Ivir gets opportunity 22.
We all have to do a consave.
Gladys and Rafross fail. Breeze and Anwynn pass and get to halve it. Ivir succeeds and can quarter it.
First half, 33 damage, halved to 16.
Second half 37 damage, halved to 18.
Gladys goes down,
Anwynn moves over to Gladys, then Hex’s Gaia’s strength and uses eldritch blast for 12 damage. She responds to it as if it was far more.
Anwynn succeeds a deception check to hide their inner thoughts from Gaia.
Breeze heals Gladys and attacks the wall with acid splash for 7 damage.
Ivir reckless attacks the wall, for 25 on the first attack and gets a thread. Rolls 26 with athletics to snap the string.

The Wall Crumbles

Anwynn fails a deception check against Gaia, she stares straight at them as the wall falls apart. I see recognition in her eyes.
Gaia stares into Breeze’s soul and says “The gifts of my father will not help you fight me”, not talking about the shards.
Gaia glances at Rafross’ tattered broken hand wraps and they fall apart in tatters, “You could have been so great if you hadn’t abandoned the boons given to you, good luck finding any other being to grant more to you”.
She turns to Ivir, taking in the flaming glaive and the power in Ivir’s hands with a look of hunger on her face. “The destruction of my mother will not protect you”. “Destruction” being the fire that consumes.
She looks towards Gladys but doesn’t know what to make of her. “I see the touch of my father in you but I don’t think that’s your path. We shall meet again”.
“You have opened the door, you cannot close it, the gifts of my father shall not bind me, and I shall free my mother.”
Turning to Anwynn she says “And I shall destroy my brother no matter how many parts he breaks himself into”

dnd/dnd-2025-11-23-session-notes.title: November 23, 2025 - Session Notes
dnd/dnd-2025-11-23-session-notes.content:
Recap

Fought and beat Kisha/Gaia.
Fought a big defensive war against the oncoming army, evacuating all the refugees to the other side of the wall.
Took out almost all enemies, but two large seige engines are standing but inoperable.
Wall was almost entirely destroyed following a BETRAYAL BY ELGA, who opened the gate mid battle.

Pursuing Elga through the keep

Needing to peruse Elga to ensure that she doesn’t return to the tabaxi and ruin Breeze’s cover story.
Annwyn used psychic lance which gave an indication of what direction she was.
Settle on a plan to have Gladys and Rafross wait near the exit to spot her if she leaves.
While they’re waiting, Annwyn and Breeze wait sneakily to spot her moving.
Ivir feels furious at the betrayal, and letting go any restraint, we see him gain a glowing red aura, and the glaive has iron flakes fall off, and it takes on a cracked magma.
Kisha’s words about “my mothers rage” spring to mind.
Ivir is using divine sense/detect magic to search for Elga, his vision has gone hazy red, in his vision of red he sees a ghostly blue shape moving through on the other side of the wall, not an extraplanar being, but there are extraplanar objects in the same area.
Ivir, despite knowing that there’s a wall between him and the blue shape, explosively rages and attempts to power straight through the wall and any obstacles.
Crits on attack role, and the wall is obliterated to molten rock by the magical red glowing glaive as he charges straight through.
Immediately upon entering that room he’s blasted with some kind of gritty poisonous something, that he manages to not get effected by.
Charges right up to where Elga is, though she’s in cover.
Attacks the rock she’s taking cover behind and destroys the cover, but doesn’t hit her at all.
She runs and lays traps.
We pursue, managing to pick up her tracks after repeatedly hiding.
Breeze has cast detect thoughts and discerns that she’s driven by fanatical devotion and is otherwise calm and prepared to die for her god.
Rafross grapples her, but she throws down smoke bomb that knocks out Ivir and Rafross.
Anwynn has levitated and is hovering near the ceiling and watches as she flees out that gatehouse.
Anwynn uses minor illusion to create a voice of a Kishar priest calling out for her help to escape, emitting from a pile of bodies.
This convinces her, and she immediately places highest priority on finding and helping the priest.
After luring her back within range, Ivir misses with some thrown rocks.
Breeze incapacitates her with Tashas Hideous Laughter.
Rafross grapples her, she’s incapacitated, grappled, and tied up with rope with a DC 23 check on the quality of the knots/bindings.
Ivir walks over and kicks her, knocking her out of the laughter, levels the molten glowing glaive at her throat and asks “where is Ursula, what did you do to her!? Why did you do this? We were ready to help you and your people and you betrayed us!”
She says in response “What could you do that a god can’t”
Breeze has detect thoughts and picks up “Who the fuck is Ursula” then confusion because it doesn’t compute that her people need help or are danger at all.
Breeze shouts out to Ivir that “she doesn’t remember the bear”
Ivir knocks her with the butt of the glaive and says “The bear I sent with you”
Breeze detects her thoughts as “why would I keep that around” and that she didn’t kill the bear, but her being confused that he would care more about an animal than anything else. Also picks up that she killed the human spies she was sent to communicate with.
Rafross takes the holy symbol away from her, and as he does she says incredulously “you fools, did you really expect this to be ‘proof’ of anything”
Rafross retrieves two potions of pocket sand (blinding), one essence of ether (unconsciousness), four poison darts (torpor) + one no longer poisonous dart from his neck.
Breeze asks if her people are fanatics as well.
He picks up on her thoughts of her counting in her mind, because she’s realised that he’s detecting her thoughts and she’s trying to counter it.
He pushes deeper, and she knows that he’s pushing deeper into her thoughts.
He catches that no the whole village aren’t fanatics, but gets the image of the faces of four gnomes but no names.
Ivir questions Kishars power, tells her that we are more powerful.
She responds “She will free our world, she is the shield that will break the way open to new worlds”
Breeze picks up that she’s completely contemptuous of these questions and nothing is coming close to questioning her devotion.
Annwyn asks Ivir to leave to go search for Ursula while we wait for reinforcements to take her prisoner.
Annwyn also mentions what Kishar said about being part of Kishars brother and maybe that’s useful.
Breeze picks up on her thoughts about “Kishars sibling, Anshar, the reflection and complete opposite. Kishar is the earth and Anshar is the Horizon. Anshar is the barrier to leave for Kishar”
Anshar is a barrier in the way of leaving the earth, but she doesn’t have any planar understanding.

Ivir walks off into the forest, the feeling of rage slowly leaving his body, a primal animalistic feeling of retreat to a quiet dark place. Feeling embarrassed and regretful about getting caught up in rage and attacking his friends. Feeling the weight of actually having friends and a place for the first time with exile, and that Annwyn took the care to give him a moment of relief. He takes a moment to purge the poison from his body, and preparing for the worst and anticipating the site of a massacre moves forward, speaking to the animals of the forest to get what information he can. Feelings of failing so utterly his original home and village, while simultaneously having succeeded at protecting all these people that he had so little connection to. The knowledge that fighting to let the refugees through the gate led to four fanatics being granted entry weighs heavily on him.
Walking through the forest he comes upon three of the humans killed by Elga, with signs of a fourth further into the undergrowth. Amongst them, he see’s the face of Costa, covered in grime and tears. Using the last of his strength, Ivir heals him and brings him back from the edge. Almost non-verbal, he manages to tell Ivir how much he wanted to help, how much he hated being told that it was never the right time, how he pushed himself to the brink to get here in time to help and arrived just too late to save any of the humans. Ivir holds him and apologises for failing them all, for letting them down, for trusting the wrong person and feeling responsible for these deaths.
Ivir throws Costa over his shoulder and asks if he’ll come and help look for Ursula. Costa immediately holds tightly, clinging onto him as a beacon of hope.
From the animals he learns that Urusla is fine and has gone back to her natural behaviour.
He turns his attention to digging graves for the fallen humans.

index.title: Seren.Monster
index.content: This is a page for any thoughts/reviews/ideas that need somewhere more suitable than social media. This is my cat Dr Scrappy Monster MD.

movie-log/azrael-2024.title: Azrael (2024)
movie-log/azrael-2024.content:
4/5
Really excellent, incredibly innovative. Minimal in interesting ways that apparently didn’t work for some people but I loved it.

movie-log/be-natural-the-untold-story-of.title: Be Natural The Untold Story of Alice Guy-Blaché (2018)

movie-log/dawson-city-frozen-time-2016.title: Dawson City: Frozen Time
movie-log/dawson-city-frozen-time-2016.content:
5/5
Amazing documentary about a trove of silent films on nitrate that had been abandoned and buried in landfill since the late 1920’s. Using the salvaged silent films to construct a visual telling of the story of the documentary. Best documentary I’ve seen in a long time.

movie-log/die-monster-die-1965.title: Die Monster! Die! (1965)
movie-log/die-monster-die-1965.content:
5/5
Truly excellent adaptation of The Colour out of Space, let down by the most unrepresentative title imaginable.

movie-log/fallen-1998.title: Fallen (1998)
movie-log/fallen-1998.content:
4/5
Excellent Denzel Washington film from the late 90s typifying the overwhelming religious christian anxiety in the lead up to 2000.

movie-log/flesh-and-fantasy-1943.title: Flesh and Fantasy 1943
movie-log/flesh-and-fantasy-1943.content:
3/5
Interesting anthology of horror-ish supernatural-ish stories from 1943. A lot of inevitable problems regarding race and attitudes towards women that show up in anything from the US in the 40’s, but otherwise pretty well done. Definitely one of the better things from this period that I’ve seen.

movie-log/golden-ninja-warrior-1986.title: Golden Ninja Warrior (1986)
movie-log/golden-ninja-warrior-1986.content:
2/5
A Godfrey Ho movie, you know what you’re gonna get and you get it. Continues the tradition of about 30 seconds of abrupt wrap-up before cutting to credits.

movie-log/goliath-and-the-vampires-1961.title: Goliath and the Vampires (1961)
movie-log/goliath-and-the-vampires-1961.content:
2/5
Perfectly serviceable pepplum movie, gorier effects than I would have expected from the time.

movie-log/last-of-the-gladiators-1988.title: Last of the Gladiators (1988)
movie-log/last-of-the-gladiators-1988.content:
2.5/5
Evel Knievel truly is a disgusting piece of shit. Openly describing his violent lynching fantasies to camera and then describing how he settled for viciously attacking the guy and breaking his arms with a baseball bat because he wrote a book that Knievel signed off on without reading and then hated. All the crashes and injuries are nice schadenfreude.

movie-log/lone-star-1996.title: Lone Star (1996)
movie-log/lone-star-1996.content:
2/5
Potentially amazing film looking at contemporary American life in all its ugliness, ruined by an incredibly off putting final scene incest reveal.

movie-log/longlegs-2024.title: Longlegs-2024
movie-log/longlegs-2024.content:
1/5
Incredibly dissapointing, had so much potential and loved its presentation and style and the narrative pacing. But could have been so much more than yet another christian devil horror movie.

movie-log/sinners-2025.title: sinners-2025
movie-log/sinners-2025.content:
3.5/5
Really solid, interesting stuff with the comparisons drawn between Irish oppression by the English and American slavery. Didn’t land 100% for me. Felt very much like a “party movie” in the way 60s beach movies or Bollywood movies are party movies.

movie-log/stone-1974.title: Stone (1974)
movie-log/stone-1974.content:
4.5/5
Really excellent crime/drama from Australia about bikie gangs and the underclasses in Sydney in the 70s.

movie-log/strange-days-1995.title: Strange Days (1995)
movie-log/strange-days-1995.content:
5/5
Masterpiece, Perfect. Only a woman could have made this. All of the shots of men experiencing others experiences when hooked up to the wire perfectly capture a horror of arousal that I’ve never really seen portrayed before. Ralph Fiennes was fantastic, almost didn’t recognise him
P.S Pretty sure I saw a very young Jason Tobin in one of the street montage shots right at the beginning.

movie-log/the-bat-1926.title: The Bat (1926)
movie-log/the-bat-1926.content:
3/5
Nothing special by today’s standards, though it precedes batman by a decade at least and the costume is similar, there’s a plot point similar to Jokers very first introduction, and a bat signal. But who can say really whether there was any influence.
Felt kinda wild/surreal (even though it makes complete sense) to be watching a film that’s nearly 100 years old.

movie-log/the-boy-and-the-heron-2023.title: The Boy and the Heron (2023)
movie-log/the-boy-and-the-heron-2023.content:
5/5
Excellent from Studio Ghibli as always. Profound reflection on the nature of Imperial Japan and how despite the intentions of everyone who constructed it, the only way for anything better to exist was for it to burn.

movie-log/the-exorcist-3-1990.title: The Excorcist 3
movie-log/the-exorcist-3-1990.content:
4.5/5
Excellent film, think this worked for me a lot more effectively than the first one. Amazing Bunch Of Guys (character actors) given fantastic material to work with. In spite of the glut of christian horror in recent years which always just feels stale and disappointing (see longlegs-2024) this didn’t have that problem at all. Looking forward to seeing the Legion directors cut version sometime soon.

movie-log/the-french-connection-1974.title: The French Connection (1974)
movie-log/the-french-connection-1974.content:
4.5/5
Excellent as always, had been a while since I’d seen it but had in no way diminished.

movie-log/three-days-of-the-condor-1975.title: Three Days of the Condor (1975)
movie-log/three-days-of-the-condor-1975.content:
5/5
They really don’t make them like this any more. No gimmick, no weird thing to make it stand out. Just an excellent story about an interesting time and place, with a whole bunch of excellent Guys. Loved it.

movie-log/were-all-going-to-the-worlds-f.title: We're All Going To The Worlds Fair (2021)
movie-log/were-all-going-to-the-worlds-f.content:
4/5
Unnerving and thoughtful coming of age via horror story. Very much about the types of connection that exist online, the unknowability of others and uncertainty of every connection, but simultaneously how important those connections can be nonetheless. The particular kind of pain of having no other means of contact and being left at times grappling with loss because someone just disappeared. Loved it.

music/index.title: Music
music/index.content: Somewhere for any music I might make to go.

music/modul-ls48.title: Modul LS 48
music/modul-ls48.content:
Not wholly original, primary 9 note sequence is from Nik Bärtsch’s Ronin, Lyria, Modul 48.
Composed using Braid with code shown below. Functions defined at the end are used to trigger changes in the live performance. Recorded live in VCVRack 2.
from braid import *

tempo(40)
custom_scale = Scale([0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10])

def x():
    return choice([2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10])

stop()
clear()

t1 = Thread(1)

notes/notes-on-hayeks-bastards.title: Notes on Hayeks Bastards
notes/notes-on-hayeks-bastards.content:
Citation 
                  
                

Type: book
Title: Hayek’s Bastards: Race, Gold, IQ, and the Capitalism of the Far Right
Author: Slobodian, Quinn
Year: 2025
Publisher: Princeton University Press


Highlights
Introduction

From this perspective, neoliberalism can look like a recipe book, a panacea, and a one-size-fits-all nostrum. But the writings of neoliberals themselves offer a different picture—and this is where we must go to make sense of the apparently contradictory political manifestations. When we do, we discover that neoliberal thought is not filled with solutions but with problems. Can judges, dictators, bankers, or businesspeople be reliable guardians of economic order? Can institutions be made, or must they grow? How can markets be accepted by people in the face of their frequent cruelty?40 Radnitzky captured the puzzle well in the epigraph to his paper from the MPS meeting in Munich. It was from Anthony de Jasay: “Democracy’s last dilemma is that the state must, but cannot, roll itself back.”



“Since the political surprises of the Brexit vote and Trump’s victory in 2016, there has been a stubborn story that explains so-called right-wing populism as a grassroots rejection of neoliberalism, often described as market fundamentalism, or the belief that everything on the planet has a price tag, borders are obsolete, the world economy should replace nation-states, and human life is reducible to a cycle of earn, spend, borrow, die. This “New” Right, by contrast, claims to believe in the people, national sovereignty and the importance of culture. As mainstream parties lose support, the elites who promoted neoliberalism out of self-interest seem to be reaping the fruits of the inequality and democratic disempowerment they sowed.
But as this book helps make clear, this story does not capture the whole truth. By looking more closely, we can see that important factions of the emerging Right were, in fact, mutant strains of neoliberalism. The parties dubbed as right-wing populist, from the United States to Britain and Austria, have rarely been avenging angels sent to smite economic globalization. They offer few plans to rein in finance, restore a Golden Age of job security, or end world trade. “By and large, the so-called populists’ calls to privatize, deregulate, and slash taxes come straight from the playbook shared by the world’s leaders for the past thirty years.31
Even more fundamentally, to understand neoliberalism as an apocalyptic hypermarketization of everything is both vague and misleading. As many histories now show, far from conjuring up a vision of capitalism without states, the neoliberals gathered around the Mont Pelerin Society founded by Hayek (who used the term “neoliberalism” as self-description into the 1950s) have reflected for nearly a century about how the state needs to be rethought to restrict democracy without eliminating it and how national and supranational institutions can be used to protect competition and exchange.32 When we see neoliberalism as a project of retooling the state to save capitalism, then its supposed opposition to the populism of the Right begins to dissolve.”



Some saw neoliberalism as a matter of designing the right constitution, others saw a constitution in a democracy as—in a memorably gendered metaphor from de Jasay—“a chastity belt whose key is always within the wearer’s reach.”



This book shows that many contemporary iterations of the Far Right emerged within neoliberalism, not in opposition to it. They did not propose the wholesale rejection of globalism but a variety of it, one that accepts an international division of labor with robust cross-border flows of goods and even multilateral trade agreements while tightening controls on certain kinds of migration. As repellent as their politics may be, these radical thinkers are not barbarians at the gates of neoliberal globalism but the bastard offspring of that line of thought itself. The reported clash of opposites is a family feud.

Chapter One

In a 1976 lecture in Australia that he would reprise two years later in apartheid South Africa, titled, “the atavism of social justice,” Hayek said, “Socialists have the support of inherited instincts, while maintenance of the new wealth which creates the new ambitions requires an acquired discipline which the non-domesticated barbarians in our midst, who call themselves ‘alienated,’ refuse to accept although they still claim all its benefits.”7 The urgency for Hayek was his concern that the pursuit of such a program could ultimately lead to mass death. It was only by adhering to a “game” that “pays so little attention to justice but does so much to increase output” that a growing world population could sustain itself.8 Mass mutual indifference was the secret to sustaining human civilization.



Hayek seemed to demand something elusive: a small group without the group feeling that might move in the direction of sharing, a society absent of demands for social justice, a troop with no impulse toward redistribution: communal cohesion without a sense of community.



For conservatives like Minogue there was also the concern that Hayek was instrumentalizing religion and tradition. Beginning in the early 1980s, Hayek made ever more reference to the need for morality as an anchor for market order. As Wendy Brown and Jessica Whyte have written, it was “markets and morality,” not markets in the place of morality, that became his central theme.22 Yet the way he talked about religion was enough to give a conservative pause. It was hard to shake the impression that Hayek saw morality as having little meaning for its own sake. He conceded this himself when he said that “we have to recognize that we owe our civilization to beliefs which I sometimes have offended some people by calling ‘superstitions’ and which I now prefer to call ‘symbolic truths.’”23 Why were these symbolic truths important and how had they prevailed in long-term processes of cultural “selection”? They facilitated the competitive order. “Our morals,” he wrote, “the morals which have prevailed, the morals of private property and honesty, are simply those that favor the practices that assist the multiplication of mankind.”24



This meant that “the capitalist society, with its cosmopolitanism, its judgement of worth by results, and its acceptance of consumer choice, is in some ways unnatural and therefore always precarious.”27 An alliance with conservatives over religion and tradition made sense, even strategically, as an insurance policy against the atomizing and disrupting effects of untampered market competition.

Chapter Two

Rothbard conscripted the Austrian economist and his mentor Ludwig von Mises for his argument, quoting him as asserting in 1922 that “primitive man lacks all individuality in our sense. Two South Sea Islanders resemble each other far more closely than two twentieth-century Londoners. Personality was not bestowed upon man at the outset. It has been acquired in the course of evolution of society.” Rothbard believed that the egalitarianism of the 1960s New Left was both “antihuman” and “evil.” It sought to strip mankind of the fruits of civilizational advancement, namely, the emergence of individuality and human diversity. The economist Karl Polanyi, too, was criticized for his “worship of the primitive.” Because humans were unequal, some were simply more gifted than others. Elites must be respected: “the only sensible course is to abandon the chimera of equality and accept the universal necessity of leaders and followers.



To Rothbard, the egalitarian challenge to the natural inequality of ability and differences of sexuality and gender would lead to “the destruction of civilization, and even of the human race itself.” “The egalitarian revolt against biological reality” was “only a subset of a deeper revolt: against the ontological structure of reality itself, against the ‘very organization of nature’; against the universe as such.

notes/uni-layoffs-june-2025.title: University Layoffs and the Loss of Institutional Knowledge
notes/uni-layoffs-june-2025.content:
On June 3rd 2025 my University announced a fresh round of layoffs and course cuts to save 15 million. You could be forgiven some confusion walking around a campus littered with brand new gleaming steel and glass buildings and the accompanying billions in debt.
It feels upsetting to have to state something so obvious, but the living core of a university — more than any building or space — is the people that inhabit it. They are the blood from which all else is given life. But to think of them only as a number or a population is to miss the most important piece; the institutional knowledge that they carry. To stretch the analogy, blood is meaningless if it’s the wrong type, if it lacks oxygen. Sure it might Keep you on your feet for mother hour or two but that’s still a death sentence, just delayed.
Institutional knowledge lives and breaths slowly; not as an animal but as a forest. A complex ecosystem in which the embodied experience of an individual can be shared and critiqued and metabolised by those who are younger parts of the ecology. While it may feel counter intuitive that the occupation of knowledge production be so sedate — given how the most important aspect is collating and communicating that knowledge — as anyone who’s tried to learn a new language, or to play an instrument knows, the skills and the outputs are very different things.
Business doesn’t operate this way. While there are obviously complexities that are beyond my expertise, there are in general inputs that need processing by skilled workers to produce outputs. The skills can be taught and certified; and one employee can, without enormous trouble, take the place of another.
To run a lab like this — and I imagine any other research endeavour — is to doom the project to a revolving door of postdocs who spend tens of thousands to set up new experiments, publish a paper or two after the 1-2 years it takes to get up and running, before moving on without passing anything on so the cycle can repeat. If they’re lucky, maybe the PhD students doing the tedious work will have a reliable CI (chief investigator, leads research groups) higher up the chain so they don’t waste 3+ years for nothing.
We’re already 90% of the way there, but that’s no reason to give up and roll over.
These attitudes have been decimating the arts for far longer than the sciences; but not even the disciplines — like quantum — that have significant public and industry investment, are safe. In fact the amount of investment means that universities are only going to bleed researchers to industry because when they don’t care to support them appropriately, why stay…
The university is the campus of beautiful new buildings built with 1.5 billion dollars of debt. The staff with decades — and potentially centuries — of collective experience are chips to be gambled away for 15 million in immediate returns. The course catalogue that consistently generates millions in profit is to be gutted because the profit margins can’t be squeezed further when the material requires face to face learning. The students are meat to be processed into accredited assets to be used in service of capital, while the university extracts every cent it can in the form of governmental subsidised debt, no risk required.
None of this is inevitable. Government could properly fund research and higher education. Higher education is one of Australia’s most important exports, and one of the only industries that represents what Australia could be without resource extraction or tourism. The NTEU is theoretically powerful in terms of the potential impact coordinated industry wide action could have. They could use that power to push for change. Till now they’ve been content to soften the blow with minor concessions on a case by case basis each time a new round of layoffs or bargaining are announced at another university. They’ll only fight if we make them.
